note: Language-agnostic conformance vectors for ADR 0007 certifiable stratified negation (SOUND redesign). Polarity-tagged body literals, Neg premises discharged against sealed closed-model certificates, the closed_world cert list, AND the sound-verifier obligations: a DERIVED bound context (recomputed program_hash + fixed non-zero profile/ctx/theory pins), an EDB-of-record snapshot binding (s3.6), trusted whole-program closure (s3.3), scope downward-closure (s3.2), domain coverage (s3.4), rank consistency (s3.5). Authored by hand from ADR 0007 + the 6 adversarial exploits (each MUST reject). NOTATION (extends check.json): body literal = bare goal {pred,args} (positive) | {neg:<goal>}. premise = bare int (positive node) | {neg:{atom:<lit>, cert:<int>, nonmember:'direct_lookup'}}. A derivation carries closed_world:[cert...]; each cert = {scope:{level,predicates:[pred...]}, domains:[{type_tag,values:[term...]}], extensions:[{pred,arity,rows:[lit...]}], supports:[{fact,clause,subst,body_refs:[{same_stratum:{fact,rank}}|{lower_stratum:{cert,atom}}|{builtin:{atom}}|{neg_lower:{cert,atom}}],rank}], limits_decl:{...}}. CONTEXT BINDING (driven by the CLI): the bound context is DERIVED from the live program (recomputed program_hash) + fixed pins; each cert is auto-bound to it UNLESS the cert sets an explicit program_hash/profile_hash/ctx_hash/theory_config_hash (the mismatch cases). A case with 'plain_check':true calls the plain check() (unbound zero context) for cert_context_unbound. A case may set 'cert_context':{pin overrides}. Top-level 'extensional' lists EDB predicates; 'edb' supplies their EDB-of-record rows (the s3.6 snapshot). The negation_v1 profile: lt theory (lt(a,b) Holds iff a<b bytewise); EDB leaves = the 'extensional' set; Context = unit. Rows that state a `report` pin check()'s work counters tri-core (#4206): counters_version and all 17 counters of the fresh check (never a memo pass), hand-computed from the counting rules in contract/rs/src/check/report.rs, never pasted from an implementation. PINNED vs COUNTED (#4206, the coordinator's rule: never pin by hand a value the checker's own order of work decides). A report value is either an integer, pinned exactly, or the string "counted", which asserts the counter is counted (a non-negative integer) without pinning its value. Pinned wherever report.rs's rules fix the value from the row's derivation, program and profile: the walk's counters (nodes_walked and the three kinds, premises_pos/neg, theory_decisions, leaf_verifications, admissibility_checks, max_depth_reached, max_term_depth_reached) and certs_verified; and, on a row whose certificate is verified to completion, the certificate meters (cert_tables_read, cert_rows_read, join_steps_used, groundings_enumerated), which are then totals over the certificate's own tables and closure. A row whose certificate is refused partway (cert_canonical_rows_unsorted) states those four as "counted": how much was read before the refusal depends on the order the checker visits tables. check() Outcome equality compares the verdict only (checker SPI v2), so this report pin is the only place the counters are compared. No vector row exercises certs_memo_hits: a memo hit needs a second check of one world, which no row is.

cases.name: neg_atom_present_reject
cases.note: q :- \+ denied(s2). denied(s2) IS sealed-present in the exact denied table, so \+ denied(s2) is FALSE.

cases.name: accept_negation_of_absent_atom
cases.note: qa :- \+ denied(s1). denied(s1) is ABSENT from the exact sealed denied table {denied(s2)}, so the negation holds and qa accepts. The cert is bound (derived context) + EDB-matched.

cases.name: c3_support_ref_cites_missing_cert
cases.note: #2258 C3: identical to accept_negation_of_absent_atom EXCEPT the support edge's lower_stratum ref cites cert 7 in a one-cert closed_world. Before C3 the checker never read the ref's cert index and resolved it against the current cert, so this ACCEPTED. The cited index is out of range, so the cited cert is invalid, and the Neg premise citing it is rejected cert_out_of_range.

cases.name: c3_support_ref_cites_another_cert
cases.note: #2258 C3: two identical, individually valid certs. Cert 1 cites its own index. Cert 0's lower_stratum ref cites cert 1, an EXISTING cert that also holds revoked(s2). Resolving against another cert's table is sound only once that cert is known Valid, so until stacked certificates (#2258 (a)) any index other than the ref's own is refused. Cert 0 is invalid, and the Neg premise citing it is rejected cert_unsupported. Control: accept_negation_of_absent_atom, where the ref cites its own cert 0.

cases.name: c3_support_ref_own_nonzero_index_accepts
cases.note: #2258 C3 control: the rule is that a ref cites its OWN cert, not index 0. Two valid certs; each one's lower_stratum ref cites its own index (0 and 1), and the Neg premise cites cert 1, which is valid, so qa accepts.

cases.name: cert_canonical_scope_unsorted
cases.note: issue #839 (canonical-form gate 1b) — identical to accept_negation_of_absent_atom EXCEPT the sealed scope predicates are authored in NON-canonical order (revoked before denied; symbol byte order puts denied first). The cert collections carry a sorted+deduped invariant that rs/go binary-search against; gate 1b rejects a violating cert deterministically, before any membership lookup. DISCRIMINATOR: a binding whose vector loader canonicalizes on construction (the pre-#839 go/ts loaders) silently repairs this cert into the valid one and ACCEPTS — the loader must carry the authored order verbatim for this case to mean anything. go+ts replay; rs pins the same gate programmatically in contract/rs/tests/negation.rs.

cases.name: cert_canonical_domain_unsorted
cases.note: issue #839 (canonical-form gate 1b) — identical to accept_negation_of_absent_atom EXCEPT the finite domain values are authored in NON-canonical order (s2 before s1). This is the consumer-measured hazard shape: every correct value present, only the ORDER wrong, and rs/go binary-search membership then reports present values absent per lookup luck (an arbitrary cert_out_of_domain). Gate 1b rejects deterministically with the same code and a detail naming the real cause. Same loader DISCRIMINATOR as cert_canonical_scope_unsorted: a canonicalizing loader repairs this into the valid cert and wrongly ACCEPTS.

cases.name: cert_canonical_rows_unsorted
cases.note: issue #839 (canonical-form gate 1b) — the denied extension carries TWO rows authored in NON-canonical order (denied(s2) before denied(s1); ground-key order puts s1 first). rs/go binary-search table membership, so unsorted rows defeat the sealed-table lookups that support/closure/negation all rely on; gate 1b rejects deterministically (cert_unsupported — the code a defeated membership scan would otherwise fabricate) with a detail naming the real cause. Same loader DISCRIMINATOR as cert_canonical_scope_unsorted.

cases.name: cert_canonical_scope_duplicated
cases.note: research 0028 A18 (#3024), duplicate handling: identical to cert_canonical_scope_unsorted EXCEPT the sealed scope predicates are SORTED with one repeated (denied, denied, revoked). The invariant is STRICTLY increasing, so gate 1b refuses a duplicate as it refuses a misorder, with the same code. DISCRIMINATOR: a loader that dedups on construction, or a check that compares with <=, silently repairs this cert and ACCEPTS. go+ts replay; rs pins the same gate in contract/rs/tests/negation.rs (reject_duplicated_scope_predicate_struct_literal).

cases.name: cert_canonical_domain_duplicated
cases.note: research 0028 A18 (#3024), duplicate handling: identical to cert_canonical_domain_unsorted EXCEPT the finite domain values are SORTED with one repeated (s1, s1, s2), and limits_decl.domain_values counts all three, so the budget step (which precedes gate 1b) agrees and gate 1b decides. The invariant is STRICTLY increasing: the same code as the misorder. Same DISCRIMINATOR as cert_canonical_scope_duplicated. go+ts replay; rs pins it in contract/rs/tests/negation.rs (reject_duplicated_domain_value_struct_literal).

cases.name: cert_canonical_rows_duplicated
cases.note: research 0028 A18 (#3024), duplicate handling: identical to cert_canonical_rows_unsorted EXCEPT the denied extension carries the SAME row twice (denied(s2), denied(s2)), sorted by ground key. limits_decl.cert_facts counts all three rows, as in the twin. The invariant is STRICTLY increasing, so gate 1b refuses the repeat with the code it gives a misorder (cert_unsupported). Same DISCRIMINATOR as cert_canonical_scope_duplicated. go+ts replay; rs pins it in contract/rs/tests/negation.rs (reject_duplicated_extension_row_struct_literal).

cases.name: term_too_deep_cert_extension_row
cases.note: issue #253 (CERT-DEEP arm) — the term-NESTING-depth cap guards a cited certificate's deep data, not just the claim/node terms (check.json's term_too_deep_tuple_arg pins ONLY the node arm). Here the sealed `denied` EXTENSION ROW carries denied(box·s2), a tuple of structural depth 2; with max_term_depth=1 the cert-deep gate (rs mod.rs §c / go check.go §c / ts checkCertTermDepths) REJECTS term_too_deep on the extension-row argument BEFORE any cert verification (the depth gate precedes verifyCert). Pins the MECHANISM via a tight limit on a shallow term — a real tens-of-thousands-deep cert term would stress each CLI's recursive decoder; the no-stack-overflow property at real depth is proven in each core's adversarial unit tests. go+ts replay this case; rs pins the same arm in contract/rs/tests/negation.rs.

cases.name: term_too_deep_cert_domain_value
cases.note: issue #253 (CERT-DEEP arm) — a sealed DOMAIN VALUE of structural depth 2 (box·s2) is rejected term_too_deep under max_term_depth=1 by the cert-deep gate's domain-value arm, after the (shallow) extension rows pass. Companion to term_too_deep_cert_extension_row; pins a second cert sub-arm. go+ts replay; rs mirrors in negation.rs.

cases.name: term_too_deep_neg_premise_atom
cases.note: issue #253 (CERT-DEEP arm, §d) — the gate also bounds a NEGATED PREMISE's ground atom (data the cert path traverses recursively). The \+ premise carries denied(box·s1) of depth 2; with the cert otherwise shallow, the gate passes (a)/(b)/(c) and REJECTS term_too_deep on the negated premise atom under max_term_depth=1, before the forward pass matches premise to clause. Pins the §d arm. go+ts replay; rs mirrors in negation.rs.

cases.name: term_too_deep_cert_support_edge_fact
cases.note: issue #253 (CERT-DEEP arm, §c support loop) — the gate also bounds each SUPPORT EDGE's justified fact. Here the edge fact is denied(box·s2) of depth 2 while the extension rows + domains stay shallow; under max_term_depth=1 the gate passes the extension/domain loops and REJECTS term_too_deep on the support-edge fact, before cert verification (so the deliberate fact-vs-extension mismatch is never reached). Pins the support-edge FACT sub-arm. go+ts replay; rs mirrors in negation.rs.

cases.name: term_too_deep_cert_support_subst_image
cases.note: issue #253 (CERT-DEEP arm, §c support loop) — the gate also bounds each SUPPORT EDGE's substitution-image terms. Here the edge subst maps S→box·s2 (depth 2) while the fact stays shallow; under max_term_depth=1 the gate REJECTS term_too_deep on the support-edge subst image (checked after the edge fact, before the body refs). Pins the support-edge SUBST sub-arm. go+ts replay; rs mirrors in negation.rs.

cases.name: term_too_deep_cert_support_ref_atom
cases.note: issue #253 (CERT-DEEP arm, §c support loop) — the gate also bounds each support edge's BODY-REF atom (the lower-stratum / builtin / neg-lower atom a body literal resolves to). Here the lower_stratum ref atom is revoked(box·s2) of depth 2 while the fact + subst stay shallow; under max_term_depth=1 the gate REJECTS term_too_deep on the support-ref atom (checked after the fact and subst images). Pins the support-ref ATOM sub-arm. go+ts replay; rs mirrors in negation.rs.

cases.name: cert_context_unbound_via_plain_check
cases.note: The plain check() supplies a zero (unbound) context; a Neg-bearing derivation is hard-rejected. Same cert as accept_negation_of_absent_atom.

cases.name: cert_context_mismatch_wrong_program_hash
cases.note: The cert pins an explicit program_hash that is not the recomputed live digest; the context override echoes it so the cert==context test passes, but the recompute test fails first ⇒ cert_context_mismatch.

cases.name: d10_slice_seal_cert_context_mismatch
cases.note: ADR 0029 D10 / gate G5 - the RED case, KEPT PERMANENTLY RED by ruling (seat:caa 2026-09-03, digest-scope errata #955/#962: a promise no release ever delivered is corrected, not narrowed). The cert is sealed over the downward-closed SLICE of the component ideal it seals ({denied, revoked}): its program_hash is program_digest of the ONE-clause program {denied_rule: denied(S) :- revoked(S)} - `revoked` is EDB and never a stratum member (ADR 0007) - NOT of the complete live program. WHY THE VERDICT IS FINAL: this cert declares NO decomposition_witness and the context is the ordinary derived one, so the checker takes the (None, _) arm and recomputes program_hash over the COMPLETE live program, which the slice pin can never equal. That is not 'today's verdict awaiting D10' - it is D10's own rule that SLICING ALONE NEVER BUYS ADMISSION: a seal is admissible only under the decomposition that authorized it, carried identically on the cert AND the bound context. The case that DOES go green under D10 is its twin `d10_slice_seal_replays_under_its_own_decomposition`, byte-identical to this one except for the witness on both sides. This case originally carried a `d10_expected: {accept: true}` landing pin and a note describing a checker that recomputes the live analysis and derives the slice per the witness - that design was refuted on contact with ADR 0004 (kernel depends DOWN on contract, so the contract-tier checker can hold neither a DecompositionWitness nor an analysis); the built design is an OPAQUE 32-byte pin compared for equality, and the field was removed rather than flipped so unit 1's red-first evidence survives. The pinned slice digest is MACHINE-DERIVED (a digest cannot be hand-authored) and drift-guarded by contract/rs/tests/negation.rs::d10_g5_vector_pins_the_recomputed_slice_digest, which rebuilds that one-clause program and recomputes it; the same guard now asserts `d10_expected` is ABSENT and the cert carries NO witness, so re-adding either reds. What each half pins, MEASURED: this REPLAY pins the REFUSAL, not the digest's identity - perturbing the pinned hex by one byte leaves the go/ts replays GREEN, because any hash that is not the live program's yields the same cert_context_mismatch (the one exception is a hex that coincides with the complete program's digest, which would ACCEPT and fail loudly here). Pinning that this hex IS the slice digest is the rs drift guard's job. Neither half is sufficient alone; that is why both exist.

cases.name: d10_slice_seal_replays_under_its_own_decomposition
cases.note: ADR 0029 D10 / gate G5 - the GREEN twin: the same slice-sealed cert as `d10_slice_seal_cert_context_mismatch` (same derivation, same pinned slice digest f1db6789..., same everything) plus the ONE thing D10 requires - the decomposition_witness carried identically on the cert AND on the bound cert_context (every other context pin stays DERIVED). Under D10 the checker takes the (Some a, Some b), a == b arm and recomputes program_hash over the SLICE the scope seals, which equals the pin, so the negation is discharged and the derivation is ACCEPTED - in all three cores, which is what G5 (2) asks for. The witness value is opaque: the contract tier compares 32 bytes for equality and never interprets them, because DecompositionWitness lives ABOVE this tier in the kernel (ADR 0004); 0xD1 x 32 is rs's own W_A fixture so the arms line up for a reader. On the wire it is an 11th TRAILING-OPTIONAL element, so the red twin still encodes to the same ten-element tuple it always did. What this replay pins: that a slice seal under ITS OWN decomposition is admitted end to end - perturbing the witness on ONE side only reds it (the different-decomposition refusal), and dropping it from the context reds it (the whole-program-run refusal). Guarded by contract/rs/tests/negation.rs::d10_g5_vector_green_twin_is_the_red_case_plus_the_witness, which asserts the two cases differ ONLY by the seal and pins the same machine-derived digest.

cases.name: exploit_closure_completeness_uncited_clause
cases.note: Lens 1. c_d2 (d(z):-base(x)) derives d(z) the cert OMITS; the old closure (support-cited clauses) never enumerated it. Trusted whole-program closure finds the missing d(z) head ⇒ cert_not_closed.

cases.name: exploit_p_implies_p_trap
cases.note: {p} is closed but unfounded; the same-stratum edge cites p at rank 0 = p's own rank 0 (consistent) but NOT strictly < 0 ⇒ cert_unsupported.

cases.name: exploit_unsealed_body_literal
cases.note: Lens 3b. deniedb(S):-base(S) where base is extensional but the cert does NOT seal it. §3.2 scope-closure rejects: a sealed-head clause body touches an unsealed, non-theory predicate ⇒ cert_scope_incomplete.

cases.name: exploit_domain_omission_builtin_ref
cases.note: Lens 4 (Round 2). flag(Y):-lt(Y,s1) with Y bound only by the builtin lt. Round-3 SAFETY gate catches the unsafe existential Y first (cert_scope_incomplete) — the precise root cause, subsuming the Round-2 cert_out_of_domain. Both are sound rejections of the same smuggled-value exploit.

cases.name: exploit_edb_omission
cases.note: Lens 5/6. The cert seals an EMPTY revoked table, omitting the live EDB fact revoked(s2). Under a bound context the §3.6 EDB gate catches it ⇒ cert_edb_mismatch.

cases.name: cert_out_of_range
cases.note: The Neg premise cites cert 0 but closed_world is empty.

cases.name: cert_budget_exceeded
cases.note: The cert declares cert_facts=2 but max_cert_facts is capped at 1 (budget gate, before any scan). Since #2335 a declared SIZE over the caller's budget is cert_size_exceeded (the caller's verify budget, kind CertSize); until CHECKER_VERSION 10 it was cert_budget_exceeded.

cases.name: cert_budget_cert_bytes_exceeded
cases.note: Trips max_cert_bytes (declared cert_bytes=4096 > budget 1). cert_bytes is the FIRST size the budget gate checks (before any scan), so it is unambiguously the first trip; all other budgets stay at their generous defaults. Reuses the well-formed q_denied_s1 cert verbatim so ONLY the budget differs. Since #2335 a declared SIZE over the caller's budget is cert_size_exceeded (the caller's verify budget, kind CertSize); until CHECKER_VERSION 10 it was cert_budget_exceeded.

cases.name: cert_budget_domain_values_exceeded
cases.note: Trips max_domain_values (declared domain_values=2 > budget 1). cert_bytes (4096) and cert_facts (2) sit under their generous defaults, so domain_values is the first budget tripped. Reuses the well-formed q_denied_s1 cert verbatim. Since #2335 a declared SIZE over the caller's budget is cert_size_exceeded (the caller's verify budget, kind CertSize); until CHECKER_VERSION 10 it was cert_budget_exceeded.

cases.name: cert_budget_support_edges_exceeded
cases.note: Trips max_support_edges (declared support_edges=1 > budget 0). cert_bytes/cert_facts/domain_values all sit under their generous defaults, so support_edges is the first budget tripped. Reuses the well-formed q_denied_s1 cert verbatim. Since #2335 a declared SIZE over the caller's budget is cert_size_exceeded (the caller's verify budget, kind CertSize); until CHECKER_VERSION 10 it was cert_budget_exceeded.

cases.name: cert_budget_rule_groundings_exceeded
cases.note: Trips max_rule_groundings via the declared-size budget gate (declared rule_groundings=1000 > budget 999), before any scan. cert_bytes/cert_facts/domain_values/support_edges all sit under their generous defaults, so rule_groundings is the first budget tripped. Reuses the well-formed q_denied_s1 cert verbatim.

cases.name: cert_budget_join_steps_exceeded
cases.note: Trips max_join_steps via the declared-size budget gate (declared join_steps=10000 > budget 9999), before any scan. cert_bytes/cert_facts/domain_values/support_edges/rule_groundings all sit under their generous defaults (rule_groundings=1000 < default 10M), so join_steps is the first budget tripped. Reuses the well-formed q_denied_s1 cert verbatim.

cases.name: cert_decl_mismatch_cert_facts_under_declared
cases.note: #2335: the cert DECLARES cert_facts=1 but seals 2 rows (revoked(s2), denied(s2)). Every budget is at its default, so the declared gate passes; the actual-vs-declared check trips: the producer under-declared, cert_decl_mismatch (engine fault), never a caller budget.

cases.name: cert_decl_mismatch_domain_values_under_declared
cases.note: #2335: the cert DECLARES domain_values=1 but carries 2 values (s1, s2). The declared gate passes at the defaults; the actual-vs-declared check trips: cert_decl_mismatch.

cases.name: cert_decl_mismatch_support_edges_under_declared
cases.note: #2335: the cert DECLARES support_edges=0 but carries 1 edge. The declared gate passes at the defaults; the actual-vs-declared check trips: cert_decl_mismatch.

cases.name: cert_decl_mismatch_cert_bytes_under_declared
cases.note: #2524: the cert DECLARES cert_bytes=1, and since CHECKER_VERSION 13 the checker MEASURES a certificate's bytes (its canonical encoding with cert_bytes zeroed). No certificate encodes in one byte, so the measure exceeds the declaration whatever its exact value: cert_decl_mismatch. Every other field is honest, and the declared gate passes at the defaults. The exact byte counts are pinned by the GENERATED vectors/cert_encoded_bytes.json, since a byte count cannot be hand-derived.

cases.name: cert_budget_precedence_declared_over_budget_and_lying
cases.note: #2335 PRECEDENCE, case 1: a liar whose DECLARATION is already over the caller's budget. It declares cert_facts=1 against max_cert_facts=0 and actually seals 2. The declared-size gate runs FIRST, because it is O(1) and must pass before anything counts the artifact (the budget bounds every later scan, including the count that exposes the lie). So this reports the CALLER's budget, cert_size_exceeded. Nothing is excused: raising the budget re-runs the check, and the lie then surfaces as cert_decl_mismatch.

cases.name: cert_budget_precedence_lie_hides_an_over_budget_size
cases.note: #2335 PRECEDENCE, case 2: a liar whose declaration is WITHIN the caller's budget while its actual size is over it. It declares cert_facts=1 against max_cert_facts=1 and actually seals 2. The declared gate passes, and the actual-vs-declared check trips: cert_decl_mismatch, the ENGINE's fault. An honest declaration (2) would have been refused as the caller's cert_size_exceeded instead; the lie is what moved it past the budget gate, so the lie is what is reported.

cases.name: round3_partition_theory_owned_in_scope
cases.note: PARTITION gate. The theory-owned builtin `lt` is sealed in scope with a FABRICATED empty table; \+ lt(0,1) reads the empty table. A stratum prefix may not seal a theory-owned predicate (builtins are decided live) ⇒ cert_scope_incomplete.

cases.name: round3_lowerstratum_intra_prefix_cycle
cases.note: LowerStratum intra-prefix ban. cp:-cq. cq:-cp. (LM={}) sealed E={cp,cq} with the positive cycle laundered as LowerStratum (rank-free) instead of SameStratum. An intra-prefix LowerStratum ref to a sealed intensional predicate is illegal ⇒ cert_unsupported.

cases.name: round3_unsafe_existential_builtin_var
cases.note: SAFETY gate. udenied(X):-src(X),lt(m,Y),lt(Y,o) has a body-only existential Y bound only by the builtin lt; the witness Y='n' lies outside the domains so closure under-fired. Y is not bound by any positive sealed-relation body literal ⇒ cert_scope_incomplete.

cases.name: round3_structural_subterm_under_fire
cases.note: Was the FUNCTION-FREE gate's case: r(box(box(X))):-e(box(X)) binds X to a STRICT SUB-term `secret` of the EDB compound box(secret), outside any whole-argument domain value, so the self-enumerating closure under-fired, and a sealed-scope clause with an open compound was cert_scope_incomplete. #2759 (seat:caa's design gate) replaced that gate with the CONSTRUCTOR-ACYCLIC one: r_struct constructs on no cycle (e is extensional), so the scope gate admits it, and the closure JOIN (#1829), which binds X by unifying e(box(X)) with the sealed row, finds the satisfied grounding and its head r(box(box(secret))), in the domain and absent from the sealed r table (the cert under-seals it) ⇒ cert_not_closed. Still rejected; the under-fire this case pins cannot recur. Its closed twin, which seals the missing row, is round3_structural_subterm_closed_accept_2759.

cases.name: round3_structural_subterm_closed_accept_2759
cases.note: #2759 (seat:caa's design gate: the CONSTRUCTOR-ACYCLIC fragment), the checker's positive arm. The same sealed scope as round3_structural_subterm_under_fire, but CLOSED: r seals r(box(box(secret))), supported by r_struct at X=secret (a DESTRUCTURED sub-term, in the domain through the support edge's subst image), and the closure join finds exactly that grounding. r_struct's head constructs box(box(X)) from e, an extensional relation, so on no dependency cycle of the scope: inside the fragment. qs :- \+ r(box(box(other))) then holds against the exact table ⇒ accept. Before #2759 the function-free gate rejected this cert cert_scope_incomplete for its open compound, closed or not.

cases.name: matcher_repeated_nested_rollback_rejects_2759
cases.note: Research 0028 row A5 (the closure matcher's completeness), #2759. mm_twin, mm(X) :- e2(twin(X, box(X))), repeats X across a NESTED tuple. The sealed e2 table holds twin(a, box(b)), whose second occurrence of X CONTRADICTS the binding X=a the first made, so that grounding fails and its binding ROLLS BACK; and twin(b, box(b)), which binds X=b consistently. This cert seals an EMPTY mm, so the closure join finds the satisfied grounding at X=b, and its head mm(b) is absent from the sealed table => cert_not_closed. A matcher that kept X=a after the contradiction misses the grounding and accepts. Its closed twin is matcher_repeated_nested_closed_accept_2759.

cases.name: matcher_repeated_nested_closed_accept_2759
cases.note: Research 0028 row A5, the closed twin of matcher_repeated_nested_rollback_rejects_2759: mm seals exactly mm(b), supported by mm_twin at X=b from twin(b, box(b)). twin(a, box(b)) grounds NOTHING, because its repeated X contradicts (X=a, then box(X) against box(b)), so the table is closed, and qma :- \+ mm(a) holds against it => accept. A matcher that bound only the first occurrence of X would derive mm(a), absent from the table, and reject this valid cert cert_not_closed.

cases.name: constructor_cycle_stratum_rejects_2759
cases.note: #2759 (seat:caa's design gate), the NEGATIVE WITNESS for its point 2: check re-derives the constructor-acyclic fragment from the BOUND program and never trusts the producer. nat_step, nat(s(X)) :- nat(X), nsmall(X), CONSTRUCTS s(X) on nat's own dependency cycle. This planted cert is otherwise VALID: the model is finite here (nsmall bounds it: nat = {z, s(z)}), both rows are supported at strictly rising ranks, and the closure join over nat x nsmall emits exactly nat(z) and nat(s(z)), both sealed; qn :- \+ nat(s(s(z))) would hold. The ONLY defect is that the sealed stratum recurses through a constructor, which the fragment excludes whatever the data (no finite table is evidence that such a model is finite) ⇒ cert_scope_incomplete, the detail naming the cycle. The mutant check that drops the constructor-cycle gate ACCEPTS this case: that is the red it exists to produce.

cases.name: adr0030_neg_over_partial_table
cases.note: ADR 0030 gate G2 - LANDED (checker version 3). Authored RED-first at b1d3d5a7 in the D10 shape: the pre-landing verdict, measured tri-core while `partial_scope` (D1: the sealed predicates whose tables are LOWER BOUNDS) was still invisible to every decoder, was "accept"; `outcome` now pins the ADR 0030 verdict. (a) `denied` is marked PARTIAL and the derivation negates it: qa :- \+ denied(s1). Today denied(s1) is absent from the (lower-bound) table, the absence is read as proof, and the case ACCEPTS. Under D2 a `Neg` premise may cite only a COMPLETE table - absence from a lower bound proves nothing, a later round could derive denied(s1) - so the verdict becomes `neg_atom_partial`, slotted between step 3 (neg_atom_not_sealed) and step 4 (neg_stratum_not_lower) of the per-Neg gate.

cases.name: adr0030_count_over_partial_table
cases.note: ADR 0030 gate G2 - LANDED (checker version 3). Authored RED-first at b1d3d5a7 in the D10 shape: the pre-landing verdict, measured tri-core while `partial_scope` (D1: the sealed predicates whose tables are LOWER BOUNDS) was still invisible to every decoder, was "accept"; `outcome` now pins the ADR 0030 verdict. (b) the same partial `denied` table cited by a COUNT: one_denied :- count(denied/1) = 1 (the clause's count slot is the ground ontos-data int 1, written in the existing tuple/atom term notation so no int form is added to any parser). Today the count recomputed over the table is 1 == k and the case ACCEPTS. A cardinality over a lower bound is itself a lower bound, never the claimed k, so under D2 the verdict becomes `count_over_partial` - the count twin of `neg_atom_partial`, kept as two codes so the band's per-premise-kind naming survives (ADR 0030 open seam, recommendation: two). First count premise in this file: the negation replays and the three conformance CLIs learned the aggregation vectors' `count_lit` / `count` forms for it.

cases.name: adr0030_partial_scope_not_upward_closed
cases.note: ADR 0030 gate G2 - LANDED (checker version 3). Authored RED-first at b1d3d5a7 in the D10 shape: the pre-landing verdict, measured tri-core while `partial_scope` (D1: the sealed predicates whose tables are LOWER BOUNDS) was still invisible to every decoder, was "accept"; `outcome` now pins the ADR 0030 verdict. (c) a "complete" table that depends on a partial one: cp :- cq, cq :- cp (least model {}), sealed E = {cp: {}, cq: {}} exact, with partial_scope = {cq} but NOT cp - cp's defining clause reads cq positively, so if cq were a lower bound cp's closure proof would be closed over E and vacuous for the rows cq is missing. D1 invariant 2 (partial-ness is UPWARD-CLOSED within the sealed prefix) rejects it by name: `cert_partial_scope_invalid`, a cert-shape refusal surfaced through the citing Neg (win :- \+ cp), like every memoized cert status. Today the field is invisible, the cert is a sound exact seal of the empty model, cp is absent, and the case ACCEPTS. The producer of D3 never mints this shape (partial = exactly the tripping stratum, nothing sealed above it); the checker verifies it anyway because a certificate is untrusted input.

cases.name: adr0030_partial_table_cited_only_positively
cases.note: ADR 0030 gate G2 - LANDED (checker version 3). Authored RED-first at b1d3d5a7 in the D10 shape: the pre-landing verdict, measured tri-core while `partial_scope` (D1: the sealed predicates whose tables are LOWER BOUNDS) was still invisible to every decoder, was "accept"; `outcome` now pins the ADR 0030 verdict. (d) the partial stratum cited ONLY POSITIVELY: the derivation proves denied(s2) with a Rule node over the partial predicate (denied_rule from the EDB leaf revoked(s2)); the cert with partial_scope = {denied} is present and never cited by a Neg. A positive premise never reads a certificate table (it resolves to a node), and every fact of a truncated bottom-up model is in the least model, so this is sound today and under the ADR: ACCEPT both ways. The control that does not flip - kept so the pair (d)/(d2) separates "the mark is ignored" from "the mark is honoured".

cases.name: adr0030_lower_bound_table_not_closed_but_marked_partial
cases.note: ADR 0030 gate G2 - LANDED (checker version 3). Authored RED-first at b1d3d5a7 in the D10 shape: the pre-landing verdict, measured tri-core while `partial_scope` (D1: the sealed predicates whose tables are LOWER BOUNDS) was still invisible to every decoder, was {"reject": "cert_not_closed"}; `outcome` now pins the ADR 0030 verdict. (d2) the case that shows what the mark BUYS: the same {denied, revoked} cert with `denied` sealed EMPTY - a genuine lower bound of the least model {denied(s2)} - marked partial, and the derivation negates only the COMPLETE table: qr :- \+ revoked(s1). Today the invisible mark leaves closure verified over `denied`, the enumeration of denied_rule derives denied(s2) which the table omits, and the cert is `cert_not_closed` (surfaced through the Neg). Under D2 closure is NOT verified for a table in partial_scope - its failure is the truth of a lower bound, not a defect - the support witness is still verified (E subset of the least model, vacuously here), the Neg cites `revoked` (extensional, never partial, complete by snapshot), s1 is absent, and the case ACCEPTS. The flip runs the safe way: a cert the checker refuses today is admitted only because it now says which table is inexact.

cases.name: accept_theory_literal_in_a_sealed_clause
cases.note: #1713 D3 — THE PIN. hot(X) :- gauge(X), lt(X, s2). is a SEALED clause whose body carries a THEORY literal, and qhot :- \+ hot(s2). negates over that sealed table from the stratum above. The checker cannot confirm the exact hot table by looking lt up in a relation — there is no lt table — so it must DECIDE lt per grounding via the pinned Theory: X=s1 gives lt(s1,s2) Holds (byte order), X=s2 has no gauge row, so the least model is exactly {hot(s1)} and hot(s2) is absent. GREEN ON ALL THREE CORES TODAY: the closure gate has always decided a theory-owned literal live, which is why #1713 was producer-tier and check()'s accept set did not move. This case is a REGRESSION FENCE against a checker that looks the literal up in a table instead, not evidence that the producer change works.

cases.name: closure_join_defers_a_leading_theory_filter
cases.note: #1829 — THE JOIN ORDER PIN (accept arm). hot2(X) :- lt(X, s2), gauge(X). writes the THEORY literal BEFORE the sealed literal that binds X. The closure gate is a JOIN over the sealed extensions: positive sealed literals BIND in declared order, and every theory or negated literal is a FILTER evaluated at the FIRST point all its variables are bound — so lt(X, s2) is deferred until gauge(X) has bound X=s1, then decided live (lt(s1,s2) Holds). Least model {hot2(s1)}, the table matches, ACCEPT. A core that evaluated the body left to right as written would meet lt(X, s2) with X unbound — either refusing it (cert_scope_incomplete) or, worse, treating a non-ground literal as false and under-firing; the sibling case below catches the second.

cases.name: closure_join_deferred_filter_fires_on_a_missing_head
cases.note: #1829 — THE JOIN ORDER PIN (reject arm, and the one that catches SILENT under-firing). Same clause hot2(X) :- lt(X, s2), gauge(X)., same gauge = {s1}, but the sealed hot2 table is EMPTY. The deferred filter lt(s1, s2) Holds once gauge has bound X=s1, so the join emits the grounding X=s1 and demands hot2(s1) in E — absent — cert_not_closed. A join that reached lt(X, s2) unbound and read it as false would emit nothing and ACCEPT a certificate whose sealed table is missing a derivable row: the exact under-fire the closure gate exists to refuse. The Neg premise \+ hot2(s2) is itself fine (s2 absent, in domain), so the rejection is the cert's, surfaced through the premise.

cases.name: closure_join_steps_counted_exactly
cases.note: #1829 — THE COUNTER PIN (join steps, exact). A join step is ONE candidate examined at ONE body literal: a table row offered to a binder, or the current tuple offered to a filter. hot2_rule over gauge = {s1}: the binder gauge(X) examines 1 row (step 1), X=s1; the deferred filter lt(s1, s2) is offered the tuple (step 2). Total 2, so max_join_steps = 2 (declared join_steps = 2, under the budget gate) ACCEPTS. Under the retired |universe|^vars odometer this clause cost 3 steps (X=s1: lt then gauge; X=s2: lt fails) and would have tripped here — the case discriminates the join's count from the enumeration's.

cases.name: cert_budget_join_steps_under_declared
cases.note: #1852 — THE DECLARATION PIN (join steps). Same certificate as closure_join_steps_counted_exactly, budgets at their defaults, but the cert DECLARES join_steps = 1 while the join PERFORMS two (the binder gauge(X) offers its one row: step 1; the deferred filter lt(s1, s2) is offered the tuple: step 2). The pre-scan gate passes (1 is under every budget); step 2 exceeds the declaration mid-join — cert_budget_exceeded, naming the field, with the scan stopped at declared + 1. Its accept twin (declared = 2 = performed) is closure_join_steps_counted_exactly, unchanged; cert_budget_join_steps_exceeded_during_closure is the budget-tripping sibling (declared 1 = budget 1), which stays a budget refusal because the budget is tested first. A core that compares the counters with the budgets only ACCEPTS this case. Since #2335 an actual count over the certificate's OWN declaration is cert_decl_mismatch (the producer under-declared, an engine fault); until CHECKER_VERSION 10 it was cert_budget_exceeded.

cases.name: cert_budget_join_steps_exceeded_during_closure
cases.note: #1829 — the join-step budget trips DURING closure, incrementally, not at the declared-size gate. Same certificate as closure_join_steps_counted_exactly with max_join_steps = 1 and declared join_steps = 1: the declared gate passes (1 is not over 1), the binder's row is step 1, and the deferred filter is step 2 — over budget mid-join, cert_budget_exceeded. Every other budget vector in this file trips at the declared-size gate before any scan; this is the one that reaches the scan. Together with its accept twin it pins the count at exactly 2 on all three cores.

cases.name: closure_join_groundings_counted_exactly
cases.note: #1829 — THE COUNTER PIN (groundings, exact). A grounding is ONE body-true tuple the join EMITS — not a point of |universe|^vars visited. hot2_rule emits exactly one (X=s1), so max_rule_groundings = 1 (declared rule_groundings = 1) ACCEPTS. The retired odometer visited 2 groundings here (X=s1 and X=s2 over the two-value domain) and refused this budget before scanning; a core still counting the grounding space fails this case.

cases.name: cert_budget_rule_groundings_under_declared
cases.note: #1852 — THE DECLARATION PIN (groundings). Same certificate as closure_join_groundings_counted_exactly, budgets at their defaults, but the cert DECLARES rule_groundings = 0 while the join EMITS one (X=s1). The pre-scan gate passes (0 is under every budget); the scan trips the moment the count exceeds the declaration — cert_budget_exceeded, naming the field. The declaration is checked against the scan's own counter AS IT RUNS, so a lying declaration is caught for this field the way cert_facts/domain_values/support_edges are caught before the scan, and the scan cost of any checked certificate is bounded by min(declared, budget): declaring small no longer walks past the gate into a full-budget scan. Its accept twin (declared = 1 = emitted) is closure_join_groundings_counted_exactly, unchanged. A core that compares the counters with the budgets only ACCEPTS this case. Since #2335 an actual count over the certificate's OWN declaration is cert_decl_mismatch (the producer under-declared, an engine fault); until CHECKER_VERSION 10 it was cert_budget_exceeded.

cases.name: closure_join_repeated_variable_binds_then_filters
cases.note: #1829 — THE REPEATED-VARIABLE PIN. same(X) :- pair(X, X). over the sealed pair = {(s1,s1), (s1,s2)}: one binder, one variable twice. The join binds X on the FIRST occurrence and FILTERS on the second — row (s1,s1) binds X=s1 and the second position agrees (emit: same(s1), present); row (s1,s2) binds X=s1 and the second position s2 disagrees (no emission). Least model {same(s1)}, same(s2) absent, ACCEPT — and the budgets are set EXACTLY at the join's counts (2 rows examined = 2 join steps; 1 tuple emitted = 1 grounding), so a core that re-bound X at the second position (emitting same(s2), absent → cert_not_closed) or that still counted the |universe|^vars odometer (2 groundings visited → over the 1 declared) fails this case by name.

cases.name: stacked_2258_m1_a_lower_cert_seals_the_negated_edb_accepts
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. The issue's own M1: cert 0 (level 1) seals stk_flag; cert 1 (level 2) seals stk_item and stk_low. stk_low's clause negates stk_flag, which cert 1 does not seal: it is read from the unique, exact, Valid certificate at a strictly lower level that seals it, and low(b)'s NegLower ref cites cert 0. Before lane 2 this was cert_scope_incomplete (neither sealed nor theory-owned). Accepted whatever Q1 ruled: stk_flag is only negated.

cases.name: stacked_2258_the_edb_sealed_once_below_accepts
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. Q1: the EDB is sealed once, in cert 0 (level 1), and cert 1 (level 2) seals only stk_low. The positive literal stk_item(X) is read from cert 0 as a closure BINDER over its rows (and binds X for the safety gate); \+ stk_flag(X) is a filter over cert 0's table. Both support refs cite cert 0.

cases.name: stacked_2258_the_order_of_the_world_does_not_matter_accepts
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. As stacked_2258_the_edb_sealed_once_below_accepts, with the upper certificate listed FIRST (index 0) and the base at index 1. Certificates are verified in ascending scope level, not index, so the base is known Valid before the upper certificate reads it.

cases.name: stacked_2258_a_three_level_stack_accepts
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. A three-level stack: cert 0 (level 1) seals the EDB, cert 1 (level 2) seals stk_low, cert 2 (level 3) seals stk_top and reads stk_item from cert 0 and \+ stk_low from cert 1. The claim stk_up(b) negates stk_top(b), citing cert 2.

cases.name: stacked_2258_equal_levels_have_no_lower_seal_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. As the edb-sealed-once-below accept, with the upper certificate at the SAME level (1) as the base. A read resolves only STRICTLY downward, so stk_item and stk_flag are sealed nowhere cert 1 may read them: cert_scope_incomplete.

cases.name: stacked_2258_a_partial_lower_table_cannot_be_read_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. As the three-level accept, with cert 1 marking stk_low PARTIAL (ADR 0030 D1: a lower bound; cert 1 itself is Valid). cert 2's sealed clause reads \+ stk_low from it, and a lower bound read by a sealed clause makes that clause's closure vacuous: cert_scope_incomplete, refused at cert 2.

cases.name: stacked_2258_an_ambiguous_lower_seal_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. Two certificates at level 1 both seal stk_item and stk_flag (cert 0 and a copy at cert 1), and cert 2 reads both. A stacked read needs a UNIQUE lower seal, decided on structure alone: cert_scope_incomplete.

cases.name: stacked_2258_a_lower_cert_with_a_wrong_pin_propagates_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. As the edb-sealed-once-below accept, with cert 0 pinning a program_hash that is not the recomputed live digest: cert 0 is cert_context_mismatch. cert 1 rests on it, so cert 1 is invalid with cert 0's OWN code (design review Q2), and the premise citing cert 1 reports it.

cases.name: stacked_2258_a_lower_cert_with_a_forged_edb_row_propagates_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. As the edb-sealed-once-below accept, with cert 0's stk_flag table carrying a row the EDB snapshot lacks (stk_flag(b)): cert 0 is cert_edb_mismatch, and cert 1, which rests on it, reports that same code. This is what keeps #2316's attribution (which fires on cert_edb_mismatch) correct in a stacked world.

cases.name: stacked_2258_neg_lower_on_a_present_atom_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. cert 1 seals stk_low = {a, b} and supports stk_low(a) with a NegLower ref to stk_flag(a) in cert 0, where stk_flag(a) is PRESENT: the negation fails, cert_unsupported.

cases.name: stacked_2258_a_cross_cert_ref_to_a_cert_that_does_not_seal_it_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. The M1 shape, with low(b)'s LowerStratum ref for stk_item(b) citing cert 0, which does not seal stk_item (cert 1 seals it itself). A cross-certificate ref must cite the certificate the predicate RESOLVED to: cert_unsupported.

cases.name: stacked_2258_neg_lower_citing_its_own_cert_for_a_lower_predicate_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). EDB stk_item(a), stk_item(b), stk_flag(a); so stk_low = {b}, stk_top = {a}, stk_up = {b}. An own-index ref resolves against the cert's own tables, as before lane 2: cert_unsupported (not sealed).

cases.name: stacked_2258_m2_an_unsealed_table_is_not_a_seal_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). A carried table is not a seal, and there is no lower certificate: cert_scope_incomplete, the real defect.

cases.name: stacked_2258_m3_one_cert_cannot_negate_its_own_seal_rejects
cases.note: #2258 lane 2 (stacked certificates, seat:caa's ruling (a), its C3 amendment and the lane-2 design review Q1-Q4). Program: stk_low(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). stk_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_low(X). stk_up(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_top(X). cases.name: law_rollback_the_matcher_restores_a_failed_rows_binding_accepts
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). MATCHER ROLLBACK, the accept arm. law_same(X) :- law_pair(X, X). over the sealed law_pair = {(s1,s2), (s2,s2)}, in canonical row order, so the FAILING row comes FIRST: (s1,s2) binds X=s1 at the first position and fails at the second, then (s2,s2) must bind X=s2 afresh. Least model {law_same(s2)}; the cert seals exactly that, and \+ law_same(s1) holds: ACCEPT. Its twin, which omits law_same(s2), is the discriminating arm. closure_join_repeated_variable_binds_then_filters puts its failing row LAST, so it cannot see a matcher that keeps a failed row's binding.

cases.name: law_rollback_a_matcher_that_keeps_a_failed_rows_binding_under_fires_rejects
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). MATCHER ROLLBACK, the discriminating arm: the same program and law_pair, and the cert OMITS law_same(s2) (the sealed law_same table is empty). A correct join undoes X=s1 after row (s1,s2) fails, binds X=s2 on row (s2,s2), derives law_same(s2) and finds it absent: cert_not_closed. A matcher that keeps X=s1 from the failed row cannot match (s2,s2), derives nothing, and ACCEPTS a table missing a derivable row: the silent under-fire the closure gate exists to refuse.

cases.name: law_a_variable_bound_only_under_negation_in_a_sealed_clause_rejects
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). AN UNSAFE VARIABLE. law_u(a) :- \+ stk_flag(X). X occurs only under negation, so no positive sealed literal binds it and the clause has no finite reading. Read existentially it would pick X=b and seal law_u(a), which is what this cert carries. The safety gate (section 3.2: an unsafe / non-range-restricted variable) refuses the clause: cert_scope_incomplete. stk_flag is sealed exactly by cert 0 at a strictly lower level, so the negated predicate is readable and the unsafe variable is the only defect. law_a_variable_bound_positively_before_its_negation_accepts is the same stack with X bound by stk_item. round3_partition_theory_owned_in_scope's r_partition also leaves X only under negation, but that case refuses the sealed builtin, so it does not pin this gate.

cases.name: law_a_variable_bound_positively_before_its_negation_accepts
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). The control for the unsafe-variable case: law_s(a) :- stk_item(X), \+ stk_flag(X). The same stack, with X bound by the positive sealed literal stk_item(X). Groundings X=a (stk_flag(a) present, no fire) and X=b (fires law_s(a)); least model {law_s(a)}, sealed exactly; \+ law_s(b) holds: ACCEPT.

cases.name: law_a_constructed_negative_lookup_in_a_sealed_clause_accepts_2759
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples), updated by #2759. A CONSTRUCTED NEGATIVE LOOKUP inside a sealed clause. law_nb(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ law_bad(box(X)). box(X) is an OPEN compound, and it sits under negation. As #3024 landed it, the function-free gate (#2294) refused an open compound anywhere in a sealed-scope clause, cert_scope_incomplete, and this case was named _rejects. #2759 (seat:caa's design gate, CHECKER_VERSION 18) replaced that gate with the CONSTRUCTOR-ACYCLIC one: an open compound in a sealed-scope BODY literal is a lookup or a destructuring pattern, and only a constructing HEAD on a dependency cycle is outside the fragment. law_box_rule's head constructs nothing. Every other obligation holds: law_bad is sealed exactly by cert 0 at a strictly lower level, the law_nb table is its least model {law_nb(b)}, and the domains cover box(a) and box(b) whole => ACCEPT. The fragment's rejecting witness is constructor_cycle_stratum_rejects_2759. The flat form is stacked_2258_m1 (stk_low's \+ stk_flag(X)), accepted.

cases.name: law_a_constructed_negative_lookup_absent_from_the_table_accepts
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). A CONSTRUCTED NEGATIVE LOOKUP at the top level, outside every sealed scope, where an open compound is allowed. law_top(X) :- stk_item(X), \+ law_bad(box(X)). With X=b the premise's atom is the constructed ground term law_bad(box(b)): it equals the grounded body literal, lies within domain e whole, and is absent from the sealed table {law_bad(box(a))}: ACCEPT. Its three twins refuse the present atom, an out-of-domain constructed value, and a lookup of the un-constructed value.

cases.name: law_a_constructed_value_outside_every_domain_rejects
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). The constructed lookup with X=b, and the cert's domains are d = {a, b} and e = {box(a)}. box(b) lies outside every domain although its leaf b lies inside d. Domain membership is of the WHOLE term (ADR 0007 section 4, obligation 5): neg_atom_ill_typed. A check over atomic leaves would accept.

cases.name: law_a_lookup_of_the_unconstructed_value_rejects
cases.note: #3024 (research 0028, advice section 5, row A17: conformance vectors for laws, not only examples). The constructed lookup with X=b, and the premise looks up law_bad(b): the variable's value without its constructor. law_bad(b) is in domain d and absent from the table, so a checker that verified the lookup without comparing it to the grounded body literal law_bad(box(b)) would ACCEPT. #2227 requires the premise's atom to equal the grounded negated body literal exactly: instantiation_mismatch.
